title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the working draft for Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (p.d.) de Rham complex. The page sits between unrelated sheets: an abandoned German letter and a 1971 typed letter about a typewriter. Grothendieck has a trigraded object C^{**}_*. For each i ≥ 0, the row C^{i*}_* is a resolution, taken in some ambient category written (SS), of an object (S^i_k)_*. The lower * is probably a simplicial index, and S^i is probably a symmetric or divided-power graded piece (i-th Hodge-type graded object). He wants the total object to compute the right thing after applying a functor τ (probably global sections, a derived-functor-type operation, or a truncation). Concretely, he wants the two natural filtrations of the double complex, horizontal (by i) and vertical (by cohomological degree), to induce isomorphisms after τ, i.e. the two spectral sequences converge correctly.

Horizontal filtration: he says it is fine because each C^{i*}_* resolves (S^i_k)_* and is 'quasi-flasque' (acyclic for τ) in a range of degrees p that grows with i. This is the standard connectivity-growth argument letting τ commute with the infinite product or limit over i.

Vertical filtration: he states a sufficient condition (4), 'probably equivalent'. For each i, let π(i) be the extremal integer such that the row C^{i·}_* is π-flasque, meaning its (bounded) component sheaves are flasque, i.e. τ-acyclic, in the relevant range. Set π(i) = +∞ if no such integer exists. Require π(i) → +∞ as i → +∞. A marginal addition rephrases this as a condition (4') on the flasque quasi-complexes.

He then states the goal: an existence and uniqueness theorem for such C^{**}_* carrying the structures above, possibly compatible with p.d. structures. This would characterise a canonical resolution model of the p.d. de Rham complex up to quasi-isomorphism, by axioms rather than by a construction. The page breaks off mid-sentence ('et satisfaisant').
errors: Possible inconsistency: π(i) is defined as the SMALLEST integer such that the row is π-flasque (with π(i)=+∞ if none), yet the requirement is π(i)→+∞. Read in the natural way (flasque from degree π onward), this would say the flasque range recedes, which is the wrong direction for convergence. The intended notion is presumably a range of acyclicity that grows with i, so either 'plus petit' should be 'plus grand' or 'π-flasque' has a non-obvious meaning.
The equivalence between condition (4) and the vertical-filtration isomorphism is only asserted ('sans doute équivalente'), not proved.
The horizontal-filtration argument is left unfinished ('donc ....'). The claim that rows are quasi-flasque in degree p for i large is marked with a question mark.

ideas.what: Convergence of both filtrations of a double complex built from resolutions of graded pieces S^i, ensured by an acyclicity or connectivity range growing with i
ideas.modern_name: Connectivity estimates for completed or Hodge-filtered derived de Rham complexes; convergence of spectral sequences of double complexes with infinitely many rows
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Cartan–Eilenberg). In the derived de Rham setting: Illusie (Complexe cotangent II, 1972), later Bhatt (2012)

ideas.what: Numerical invariant π(i) measuring the flasqueness degree of the i-th row, with the condition π(i)→∞
ideas.modern_name: Uniform growth of acyclicity or connectivity; a Mittag-Leffler / lim^1-vanishing style hypothesis

ideas.what: Wish for an existence and uniqueness theorem for multicomplex resolution models of the p.d. de Rham complex, compatible with divided-power structures
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic or universal characterisation of a canonical (derived) p.d. de Rham / crystalline complex up to quasi-isomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (derived de Rham), Bhatt (2012, derived de Rham vs crystalline), Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew (2019, saturated de Rham–Witt as initial object)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sought a uniqueness (and already existence) theorem characterising p.d. de Rham resolution multicomplexes C^{**}_* by structural axioms plus a convergence condition. This is an axiomatic 'up to unique quasi-isomorphism' characterisation, foreshadowing later universal-property characterisations of de Rham–Witt or derived crystalline complexes.
missed.quote: On aimerait trouver un th. d'unicité (i.e. déjà l'existence...) les C^{**}_* ayant les structures précédentes (au besoin compatibles avec les structures p.d.) et satisfaisant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck in 1976 already aiming at an axiomatic characterisation of the p.d. de Rham complex, in the spirit later realised by Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew. The page is too fragmentary to carry new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine convergence considerations for a filtered double complex, plus an unfinished wish for a uniqueness theorem. The wish is historically suggestive given later universal characterisations, but there is no finished, non-standard result on the page.
transcription_corrections: 'π-flasque' may be 'p-flasque', with π(i) an integer index; the letter is ambiguous in the image.
'τ' could plausibly be Γ (sections functor), given the flasqueness context.

The left-margin vertical note is only partially legible. It appears to discuss replacing or weakening condition (4) (something like '...remplacer (4) par ... affaiblir ...'), not just the line given in the transcription.
'quasi-flasque[?]' in line 4 is uncertain; it could be 'quasi-isomorphisme' or a degree-qualified flasqueness.
